newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher after late rally.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher after late rally.

text.p: COMEX copper futures sprung higher late in the day after laying dormant for most of the session, as speculators bought the market on the heels of a rally in London.
COMEX July copper rose 2.55 cents a lb on the day, to close at a new one-year high of 120.10 cents. Trades were posted from 117.50 to 120.45 cents.
Most of the buying appeared to be chart-driven, traders said, with automatic buy orders activated above last week's highs at 118.70 basis July.
Traders said a drawdown on LME inventories overnight also offered some initial support this morning. LME warehouse stocks fell by 2,750 tonnes today, after registering a 1,750-tonne drop on Monday.
In addition, dealers noted some currency-related interest from the Far East, as end-users sought to capitalize on the U.S. dollar's recent weakness.

"It was a pretty impressive price performance, but I think it was more technical with stops being triggered," said Smith Barney analyst David Rineheimer. "The question is, can it sustain these price levels?"
While stocks remain relatively tight worldwide, a seaonsal downturn in demand over the summer could limit the market's upside potential, he added.

Meanwhile, traders continued to monitor an ongoing strike at the Inco complex in Sudbury, Ontario. Workers at the plant, which produces about 90,000 tonnes of copper annually, have been on strike since the beginning of the month.
Inco officials said on Tuesday they would seek the help of a mediator to resolve the strike.
Technically, today's breach of the widely-watched 120.00 cent level opened up the opportunity to challenge one-year highs near 130 cents, analysts said.
